newsitem.title: FRANCE: 23 hurt when Paris riverboat hits Pont Neuf.
newsitem.headline: 23 hurt when Paris riverboat hits Pont Neuf.

text.p: A riverboat cruising along the Seine River hit a buttress of the historic Pont Neuf bridge in Paris on Monday, injuring 23 tourists on board but leaving the bridge undamaged, police said.
Some of those hurt suffered broken bones.
Police have opened an investigation into the cause of the accident, which took place on a clear and sunny day.
The Pont Neuf, built between 1578 and 1605, is the longest and oldest bridge spanning the Seine in the heart of the French capital. It is now undergoing restoration.
Dozens of riverboats ply the Seine, carrying tourists past the city's historic sites.

The Pont Neuf links Paris' Right and Left banks to the Ile de la Cite, an island in the middle of the Seine where the famed Notre Dame cathedral, the main city police headquarters and law courts are located.
